$comment: The recorded state of the `endora new storefront` acceptance criterion
(specs/071-modular-packaging/roadmap.md § F7). `acceptance:storefront-scaffold:ci`
compares a run to this file and fails on drift in EITHER direction: a newly-red
assertion fails, and so does a newly-green one nobody recorded. An unrecorded pass
is a criterion whose meaning moved without anybody reading it.
It landed all-green, which is unusual for an acceptance file in this repository and
is the finding rather than a formality: `acceptance:package-schema` landed red on
seven of nine because the capability it measures did not exist yet, and this one
measures a capability that turned out to be one manifest line short of working.
The roadmap named this criterion as the half that `could not be sized without
trying it` — whether a scaffolded storefront builds from packed tarballs depends on
how much of the packages' `exports` maps and `use client` boundaries survive an
install that is not a workspace link. Measured: all of it. The one thing that did
not survive was the reference storefront's own manifest, which declared none of the
eight `@tiptap/*` packages its build resolves from the workspace root.
A6 is `pass` because the job boots a backend for it. A run with no
PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL records `unmeasured` instead — never a pass — because a boot
with no backend measures the storefront's error page rather than the storefront.
If this job ever stops booting one, A6 drifts to `unmeasured` and fails, which is
the direction that keeps the headline claim honest.

history.what: the criterion landed with the command (F7 scaffold half), all six green
history.detail: A1 the copy names nothing above its own directory; A2 no `workspace:` range survives; A3 `pnpm install` outside the checkout from three packed tarballs, pinned through `pnpm.overrides` because page-builder-core's own dependency on contracts is equally unpublished; A4 every @endora-commerce/* package resolves outside the checkout; A5 `next build`; A6 `next start` answered / with 200 against a running backend.
